scoring_justification: Recomputing the OER overpotential from the agent's submitted ΔG values is unreliable given the reference's synthetic ΔG data; the verifier sandbox also cannot re-run the full DFT pipeline. Instead, the self-reported overpotential is compared to the paper's published values (0.67 eV / 0.37 eV) with threshold_or_better policy and a tolerance that absorbs legitimate toolchain spread.

hidden_assets.purpose: Hidden reference overpotential values for the perfect and oxygen‑vacancy In₂O₃ {001} surfaces
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text and DFT calculation section: overpotential 0.67 eV for the perfect surface and 0.37 eV for the oxygen‑vacancy surface.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted directly from the reported numbers in the paper's description of Fig. 6.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's own published overpotentials; they are used solely as a hidden comparison target for the reproduction task.

required.overpotential: object containing 'perfect' and 'vacancy' overpotentials in eV

outputs.description: Gibbs free‑energy diagram for the OER on perfect and oxygen‑vacancy In2O3 {001} facets, including the derived overpotentials.

output_contract.notes: All ΔG values must be given in eV, referenced to the same energy conventions. The overpotential is defined as max(ΔG₁,ΔG₂,ΔG₃,ΔG₄) − 1.23 V. The checker will verify the overpotential values against the paper's reported hidden threshold; a lower (better) overpotential meets the threshold and earns full credit.

steps.description: Self-reported overpotential for the perfect In₂O₃ {001} surface compared to the paper's reported value. Lower overpotential is better.
Self-reported overpotential for the oxygen‑vacancy In₂O₃ {001} surface compared to the paper's reported value. Lower overpotential is better.
Verify that all four ΔG fields exist for each surface, are numeric, and lie within a plausible energy range (-5 to 10 eV).
